title: Keth-seq: Sequencing-based mapping of guanine accessibility using N3-kethoxal modification
key_innovation: Compared with conventional nucleotide-specific probing approaches, Keth-seq introduces a sequencing-compatible Kethoxal modification strategy that enables transcriptome-wide mapping of guanine accessibility and RNA structures at single-nucleotide resolution.

blocks.text: How does N3-kethoxal selectively label accessible guanine bases?

blocks.alt: Principle and validation of N3-kethoxal RNA modification
blocks.legend: **Figure 1. Principle and validation of N3-kethoxal RNA modification.** N3-kethoxal selectively reacts with exposed guanine bases through modification of the Watson–Crick interface. The azide-functionalized reagent enables bioorthogonal biotinylation and enrichment of modified RNAs, while maintaining rapid cellular permeability and reversible labeling properties. These features establish N3-kethoxal as a suitable chemical probe for transcriptome-wide RNA structure mapping.
blocks.label: Keth-seq F1

blocks.text: How does Keth-seq convert guanine modification into transcriptome-wide RNA structural profiles?

blocks.alt: Transcriptome-wide RNA structure mapping using Keth-seq
blocks.legend: **Figure 2. Transcriptome-wide RNA structure mapping using Keth-seq.** Keth-seq combines N3-kethoxal modification with sequencing-based detection of reverse transcription stops. Modified guanine residues generate position-specific RT termination signals, which are normalized against controls to produce nucleotide-resolution structural profiles. The method accurately captures RNA structural features and shows strong agreement with established structure-probing approaches.
blocks.label: Keth-seq F2
